I think, also, in these references, the sources of the information were largely HVO, and the -- everything that happened appeared to be blamed on this brigade, which obviously had considerable capability and geographical spread to be doing what it was alleged to be doing. And to be honest, we tended to treat with a pinch of salt the fact that the HVO said the 7th Muslim Brigade had done things. It was quite clear that what was being done was being done by Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Well, do you remember meeting a gentleman by the name of Payam Akhavan?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Do you remember discussions with Mr. Akhavan concerning what he --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't see there's much point asking this witness about matters concerning Mr. Akhavan when Mr. Akhavan is a witness, and you can ask him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Let me just show you milinfosum number 177, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And also, the fact is that we have the evidence now about Miletici and these other matters which you put to the witnesses. Again, how does it assist us to hear it again through this witness? What is the point, apart from repetition?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Just -- well, if the Trial Chamber doesn't think that the evidence is of assistance to it, I'll willingly move on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) No, Mr. Sayers, I believe that what the President just said does a lot to clarify the situation. That is, if you are producing some evidence, you also need to show us the relevance of it as to the aim [Realtime transcript read in error "name"] that you are pursuing. I do not think we should go into history for the sake of history. This is, after all, a judicial process. So please tell us that you are pursuing such-and-such objective, and that to this particular end, you want to produce this and that. And if something was already produced or said, I do not think we need any additional repetition. And if you intend to produce something which makes part of the Defence strategy, then will you please tell the Court that. I believe we are quite clear about that. I believe that the Chamber is quite clear about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Well, if I can just put the final full stop on this particular line of questioning, there is a milinfosum that deals with this, and I would just like to ask the witness if he has seen it and to authenticate it, and I'll move on swiftly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D60/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: If it would be convenient to the Trial Chamber, I only have two questions, and that might conveniently conclude today's examination, and I'll try and be brief with Colonel Watters tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I only have two questions for you in connection with this, sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: Mr. Sayers, in the transcript, you need to show the relevance as to "the name." (Interpretation) The aim which is being pursued; it should be "aim," not "name." "Aim" which is pursued, to be corrected, because it makes no sense otherwise.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Do you recognise this as milinfosum number 177, or a copy of it, dated April the 25th, 1993?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: Yeah, it certainly looks like it, or it's similar to the sort of thing we produced.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And if you would just turn to the fourth page, there are two items I would like to cover with you on there. The first is right at the top of the page. Is it fair to say that the HVO front lines observed by the soldiers under your command ran from the villages of Dubravica to Pirici, Vidovici, and Ahmici, up to Loncari?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: Yes, I mean, I -- that would be about right, after the withdrawal following the 21st of April ceasefire agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. And when you use the word "HVO front line," what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: That was the line behind which we required the HVO to withdraw.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. So on one side there would be HVO forces and on the other side Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: Well, no, because on that line, we had asked for a zone of separation following the ceasefire of the 21st of April, which we patrolled, to just south of Zenica. Very rarely, actually, did they move much further north from the line Alpha I drew on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And then the last question is, there's a description of events at Miletici and a description or an identification of the victims. Have you ever seen this milinfosum before? Does it look familiar to you? Does it jog your memory?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: Yeah. Having read it now, I do remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And Miletici was actually behind the front lines that were established during this ceasefire period; right?

utterances.speaker: BRYAN SHAUN CHARLES WATTERS
utterances.text: I'd have to look at where Miletici was on the map, I'm afraid, to answer that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I don't think there's any dispute about where it is, Your Honour, and I think, if that's convenient, that concludes our questions for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Sayers, we have to finish this witness tomorrow. You say you don't have too much more?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I would estimate that we could be through, if we start at 9.00, Your Honour, by 10.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, will that give Mr. Kovacic enough time?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: From -- you mean until the lunch break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Until 12.00. We're adjourning at 12.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I'm rather optimistic, but please don't -- I think I will be able.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Sayers, perhaps you could arrange with Mr. Kovacic an equitable distribution, bearing in mind you've had a couple of hours already.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I will try to do that, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll adjourn now. Colonel, would you be back, please, at 9.00 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
